# Prince Tomar

> Doctoral researcher at Tallinn University. Field notes on ethnography, borders, infrastructure, and the Indian Himalaya.

## About

Prince Tomar is a doctoral researcher at the Centre for Landscape and Culture, Tallinn University (Estonia). He works with borderland communities along the Indian Himalaya — with a particular focus on road development, tracing the interplay between infrastructure, territorialisation, and the region's history, geopolitics, and terrain.

His current project studies the spatial-temporal dimensions of change in the Indian Himalaya as the pace of road development quickens. His fieldwork is primarily located in Ladakh and the Terai.

Beyond his academic work, he writes poems and is interested in the porous border between ethnography and literary studies.

## Field Sites

- [Ladakh — The Cold Frontier](https://princetomar.com/border-regions/ladakh.html): Field Site 1. Cold desert at 3500m. Road development, borderlands, and infrastructure in the Indian Himalaya. Fieldwork 2022 — ongoing.
- [Terai — A Porous Edge](https://princetomar.com/border-regions/terai.html): Field Site 2. Lowland at 80m. Cross-border mobility at the Raxaul–Birgunj checkpoint, India–Nepal border. Fieldwork 2020 — ongoing.

## Writing & Publications

- [The Field, the Border, and I](https://ethnomarginalia.com/the-field-the-border-and-i/): Essay published on ethnomarginalia.com.
- *Maker, Making, and Made: The Eventfulness of Road-building in Ladakh* — under review, HIMALAYA journal.
- *Review: Pyre (dir. Vinod Kapri)* — published in HIMALAYA journal. [DOI: 10.2218/himalaya.2025.10878](https://doi.org/10.2218/himalaya.2025.10878)
